text:
Incident Bot: paging: high GPU queue growth in customer-private-cluster (customer: AlphaFin) — autoscaler failing to scale, multiple nodetypes stuck in Init state :rotating_light:
Devon: seeing huge request queue on the private VPC cluster. 80% of inference pods in Pending or Init. Latency spikes for AlphaFin.
Maria: confirmed, dashboard shows requests queued ~650 and tail latency >12s for 99th pct. small spike for other customers but AlphaFin impacted most.
Jen (SRE): paging incoming? I see repeated kubelet heartbeat timeouts on new nodes; they never become Ready. Autoscaler logs show backoff after 3 failed node joins.
Matt: correct — autoscaler attempted 6 scale-ups in last 20m, but nodes fail to register and we hit the scale limit backoff: "scale_up_backoff_until=2026-03-15T12:31:xxZ"
Devon: can we route AlphaFin traffic to hosted fallback? They have critical SLAs.
Oncall Josh: taking this incident. I'll do immediate mitigation: route prod-inference/alphafin to hosted-cluster-us-east-1-canary for critical routes, lower rate-limits on non-critical endpoints to reduce queue.
Jen (SRE): plan A: (1) re-route critical traffic, (2) force-recreate 3 stuck nodes, (3) bump init timeout + log collection, (4) coordinate with infra team on provisioning logs.
Maria: step 1 in progress — adding routing override now. will post when active.
Ops-Bot: deploy bot: routing override applied to service=prod-inference/alphafin -> hosted-cluster-us-east-1-canary (ttl=2h) :white_check_mark:
Devon: confirmed some traffic is draining to hosted; queue dropped to ~220 but still high for other customers.
Jen (SRE): logs from node bootstrap show repeated kubelet heartbeat: "failed to send heartbeat: dial tcp <ip>:10250: i/o timeout" and cloud-init failing to fetch image due to intermittent TFTP iPXE hang.
Matt: that matches on-prem provisioning vendor heartbeat timeouts we've seen during maintenance windows — vendor agent was doing firmware rolling update. Escalating to vendor now.
Oncall Josh: I'm going to manually cordon and delete two stuck nodes to force new provisions on different hosts. Doing one at a time.
Devon: please annotate customer impact and mitigation for postmortem. AlphaFin was seeing request drops for small percent (~3%) but majority latency spike.
Jen (SRE): command I'm running:```kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending``` then```kubectl delete node <stuck-node-1>``` — will capture kubelet journal after deletion.
Matt: vendor replied — they saw NIC firmware job on host slab-12 causing PXE timeouts. They will pause job for our racks, but we still need to recover existing nodes.
Oncall Josh: node deletion 1 done. new node started provisioning; kubelet heartbeat present, pod bind progressing. Queue down to ~90.
Maria: re-checking telemetry: autoscaler still in backoff window, so it won't proactively scale beyond current in-region pool. We need to reset backoff after we confirm stable nodes.
Jen (SRE): resetting autoscaler backoff flag now and increasing node join timeout from 300s -> 600s for this cluster to tolerate slower provisioning. Patch applied.
Ops-Bot: autoscaler: backoff reset by Jen (SRE).
Devon: after backoff reset, autoscaler evaluated desired=+4 and started provisioning; two nodes passed join and pods scheduled. queue now ~18, tail latency down to ~1.2s.
Matt: vendor confirmed they paused firmware job. They will run a constrained maintenance window later.
Oncall Josh: mitigation summary: (1) routing override to hosted for critical traffic (2) manual node cordon/delete to force healthy hosts (3) vendor paused firmware job (4) autoscaler backoff reset + join timeout increased.
Devon: customers impacted: AlphaFin primary (SLAs at risk), small transient impact to 2 other customers. No data plane compromise.
Maria: capturing follow-ups: add healthcheck for iPXE/TFTP failures in provisioning pipeline, include vendor maintenance window detection to avoid overlapping firmware jobs, add metric for autoscaler "failed-join-count" to trigger alert earlier.
Jen (SRE): postmortem owners: Jen (root cause & infra fixes), Matt (vendor coordination), Maria (observability/alerting), Devon (customer comms).
Oncall Josh: I'll keep this incident open for another 2 hours to watch for regressions; if stable, we'll post handoff and close.
Devon: FYI I DM'ed AlphaFin support with temporary routing and ETA ~2h for full recovery.
Jen (SRE): saving logs:```journalctl -u kubelet -o short-precise --since "-25m" > /tmp/kubelet-1911223344.log``` and uploaded to incident bucket s3://incidents/1911223344/kubelet-logs.txt
Ops-Bot: incident ticket updated: INC-2026-1911223344 (priority: P1) assigned -> Oncall Josh.
Matt: final note: recommend lowering default autoscaler backoff threshold to avoid cascade under on-prem provisioning jitter. I'll file infra PR.
Oncall Josh: closing checklist: routing override removal plan, vendor follow-up, postmortem doc template. Will post final once done.
Incident Bot: incident status changed -> mitigated (partial) :white_check_mark:
Oncall Josh: moving to watch; if no regressions by 2h from now I'll close.
Devon: thanks team. Great fast coordination. :thumbsup:
